messages.subject: Part 1 error raw ActivPAL data
parts:
Dear all,

I’m using GGIR to process raw data from the activPAL accelerometer, and I am encountering some problems. I hope you can help me!

I’m using triaxial acceleration data sampled at 20 Hz for 8 days, 24 hours/day. File size is ~500 MB. Reading this file using the read.myacc.csv function works fine. However, when using the GGIR function I’m getting an error:


-----

Script

GGIR(datadir = "Input/Files",

     outputdir = "Output" ,

     studyname = "Test",

     mode = c(1,2,3,4,5),

     do.report = c(2,4,5),

     configfile = c(),

     overwrite = TRUE,

     do.parallel = TRUE,

    rmc.file = "110628-AP171613 202a 14Oct21 12-00am for 8d-VANE-PA08110670-AccelDataUncompressed.csv",

     rmc.nrow = Inf,

     rmc.skip = -1,

     rmc.dec = ".",

     rmc.firstrow.acc = 2,

     rmc.col.acc = 3:5,

     rmc.col.time = 1,

     rmc.unit.acc = "bit",

     rmc.unit.time = "ActivPAL",

     rmc.desiredtz = "Europe/Amsterdam",

     rmc.bitrate = 8,

     rmc.dynamic_range = 2,

     rmc.unsignedbit = TRUE,

     rmc.sf = 20,

     rmc.check4timegaps = TRUE

)

Console

  GGIR version: 2.8.2

    Do not forget to cite GGIR in your publications via a version number and

   Migueles et al. 2019 JMPB. doi: 10.1123/jmpb.2018-0063.

   See also: https://cran.r-project.org/package=GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#citing-ggir

    To make your research reproducible and interpretable always report:

     (1) Accelerometer brand and product name

    (2) How you configured the accelerometer

     (3) Study protocol and wear instructions given to the participants

     (4) GGIR version

     (5) How GGIR was used: Share the config.csv file or your R script.

     (6) How you post-processed / cleaned GGIR output

     (7) How reported outcomes relate to the specific variable names in GGIR

_______________________________________________________________________________________

Part 1

 Checking that user has read access permission for all files in data directory: Yes

Checking that user has write access permission for directory specified by argument outputdir: Yes

1

P1 file 1

Retrieving previously derived calibration coefficients

 Investigate calibration of the sensors with function g.calibrate:

 Loading chunk: 1 2Error in which(data[, 1] == 0 & data[, 2] == 0 & data[, 3] == 0) :

  'list' object cannot be coerced to type 'double'

In addition: Warning message:

In value[[jj]][ri] <- if (is.factor(xij)) as.vector(xij) else xij :

  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

 -----

Has anyone worked with raw activPAL data before and/or does anyone know how to solve this issue?

 

As an alternative, I’ve tried the same script with a compressed data filetype, which is ~120 MB. The downside to this compressed filetype is that certain data points are left out, which causes the time series to be irregular. Running the GGIR function with the compressed file does work, however. This takes about 30 minutes. Both RStudio and the files are stored locally (C:/), so processing time does not depend on network connection strength. 

Is 30 minutes of processing time normal for the GGIR function? If not, could this mean that my laptop* is struggling? And if so, could that be the reason for encountering the error I mentioned first?

 * Laptop-specs: Intel Core i7-9850H CPU @ 2.60GHz, 16.0 GB RAM


 I’m hoping someone can help me, thanks in advance!


Kind regards,

Koen van der Sluijs, MSc

Technical physician | PhD candidate

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Part 1 error raw ActivPAL data
parts:
Hi Koen,

I am back now from a long winter break...

Could you please try running the GGIR command you have with:

do.cal = FALSE
rmc.check4timegaps = FALSE

This will skip the auto-calibration and it will skip the attempt to impute time gaps in the data.

If the above works and produces a GGIR output file (in the results folder) that means that the problem is specific to either the calibration or the timegap imputations. To investigate this further, please repeat with:

do.cal = FALSE
rmc.check4timegaps = TRUE

Can you let me know the result for both approaches?
Based on this I hope to be able to pinpoint the source of the problem.

Thanks,

Vincent


Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/
